operation: Slide existing bars without rotation or deformation inside the box. Incoming 1x3 bar can use either axis orientation in this unit-bar sliding puzzle.
stronger_lower_bound: Independent enumeration of all 29 subsets of sizes 0,1,2 and all integer final translations of their bars, even allowing removal and arbitrary relocation with no path restrictions, finds no packing of an additional bar in either orientation. See independent_search.json. This strengthens the old grid-only BFS conclusion.
continuous_translation_reduction: Suppose a continuous final translated packing exists for a chosen subset and axis orientation of the incoming bar. Choose one true horizontal or vertical separating inequality for each pair of nonoverlapping rectangles and for each moving/fixed pair.

Containment and those chosen separations form independent x and y systems of difference constraints. All constants are integers because every width, height, fixed coordinate and box boundary is integral.

A real feasible difference-constraint system with integer constants has an integer feasible potential: anchor a zero node, add a super-source and use shortest-path distances, which are integers whenever there is no negative cycle. Translation by the anchored zero value preserves all inequalities.

Thus a continuous final packing would imply an integer final packing with the same orientations. The exhaustive integer static infeasibility therefore proves the at-least-three bound for continuous translations too.
construction: Slide bar0 from (0,2) to (0,0) along the empty 1x2 channel below it.
Slide bar1 from (1,4) to (0,4) left by 1.
Slide bar2 from (1,3) to (0,3) left by 1.
The vertical slot x in [3,4], y in [2,5] is now empty; place the eighth 1x3 bar there. Each slide has a collision-free swept rectangle and no bars overlap.
count: Three distinct bars. The two unit steps used for bar0 in the BFS are one length-two slide of the same bar, not two bars.
not_claimed: No proof for rotating existing bars, removing bars, deforming bars or an independently tilted incoming rectangle; those are outside the fixed-orientation sliding operation used here.
